changed.title: Parallel parity tests in cyclic window SAT force a quadratic De Morgan formula leaf cost per tag
changed.statement:
∀ d extra a q : ℕ,
  let k := d + 1
  let w := k + extra
  let m := a + 1
  let n := m * k + q * (k + 1)
  let hn : 0 < n := by dsimp [n, m, k]; positivity
  let stride := 2 ^ (w + 1)
  let I := n * stride
  ∀ F : PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.DMFormula I,
    (∀ table : Fin n → (Fin (w + 1) → Bool) → Bool,
      let inputs := fun addr : Fin I =>
        table ⟨(addr.val / stride) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩ (fun bit => addr.val.testBit bit.val)
      F.eval inputs = true ↔ ∃ word : Fin n → Bool, ∀ i : Fin n,
        table i (fun k => word ⟨(i.val + k.val) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩) = true) →
    2 ^ d * m ^ 2 ≤ F.leaves
changed.unlocks: bounds the number of literal occurrences in formulas deciding cyclic window satisfiability
changed.context: Store an accumulator and a (k-1)-bit tag. In each k-row sweep, XOR the dropped accumulator with that sweep's input for the tag, then rotate the other bits. Each padding block appends the XOR of the current k bits for k+1 rows, restoring the state. Closure tests even parity in some tag. Fix all other tags odd. The formula partitions even/odd input pairs into leaf rectangles. Neighbor pairs at a leaf form a matching, at most the square root of its area. Cauchy-Schwarz forces m^2 active leaves. Distinct tags use disjoint table addresses. Ignore window bits past k+1.

changed.title: At most 2+e private rows have distinct profiles outside a narrow column set in an AND/OR region with e at most one entry wire
changed.statement:
∀ (n m d : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
    (R : Finset (Fin n)) (B : Finset (Fin m)) (region entry : Finset ℕ) (top : ℕ),
  let raw := n + m
  let sources := R.image (fun sourceRow => sourceRow.val) ∪ B.image (fun sourceCol => n + sourceCol.val)
  let inside := fun (w : ℕ) => raw ≤ w ∧ w - raw ∈ region
  let gate := PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C
  (∀ firstRow secondRow : Fin n, firstRow ≠ secondRow → d ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun col => G firstRow col ≠ G secondRow col)).card) →
  (∀ firstCol secondCol : Fin m, firstCol ≠ secondCol → d ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun row => G row firstCol ≠ G row secondCol)).card) →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack raw C →
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C → region ⊆ Finset.range C.size → top ∈ region →
  entry.card ≤ 1 → (∀ w ∈ entry, w < raw + top ∧ w ∉ sources ∧ ¬ inside w) →
  (∀ k ∈ region,
    ((gate k).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∨
     (gate k).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or) ∧
    ∀ w ∈ (gate k).inputs, w ∈ sources ∨ inside w ∨ w ∈ entry) →
  (∀ k < C.size, k ∉ region → ∀ w ∈ (gate k).inputs,
    w ∉ sources ∧ (inside w → w = raw + top)) →
  C.output ∉ sources → (inside C.output → C.output = raw + top) →
  (B.card < d → R.card ≤ 2 + entry.card) ∧ (R.card < d → B.card ≤ 2 + entry.card)
changed.unlocks: bounds the number of private rows or columns whose profiles differ outside a small opposite set
changed.context: Fix an active outside column and vary the active private row. Until the top, outside gates cannot read a private signal, so the entry value depends only on the column. In the region each row induces a monotone unary truth table on that bit, either zero, identity or one. Without an entry there are two constant tables. Equal tables give identical outputs on every outside column, since only the top leaves the region. Fewer than d private columns cannot hide d disagreements. Count the types and exchange sides. Gate-price companions cannot exist for a bound on private inputs.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 6 bipartite graph with mask 268222 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 9 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 4) (v : Fin 6) => (268222 : ℕ).testBit (6 * u.val + v.val)) 9
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 4 by 6 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 10 AND/OR gates (three plain forms, full lines taken out, equal gates merged and unread gates dropped); at this size those forms are weak; we hold none of 9; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 9 (on paper), a gap of 1. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 3 left, 4 to 9 right, gate j writes wire 10 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 24 inputs with one vertex on each side.

changed.title: The two-lit function of the graph H on 6 points with mask 270585271 on shared wires has an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 8 gates
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 8 ∧ ∀ i j : Fin 6, C.eval (List.ofFn fun k : Fin 6 => decide (k = i ∨ k = j)) = (270585271 : ℕ).testBit (6 * min i.val j.val + max i.val j.val)
changed.unlocks: the exact size of the two-lit-points function of this graph on six shared wires; the family shows where a NOT gate pays with no equal lines
changed.sketch: We hold a circuit of 9 gates, a weak hand form (best over a few point orders and the complement plus a NOT, equal gates merged): OR(0,1), NOT(6), AND(5,7), OR(4,6), AND(3,9), AND(2,4), OR(8,10), OR(11,12), NOT(13) (inputs 0-5 are the points, gate k is wire 6 + k, output last). We hold no circuit of 8 gates; this is a search. No complete search of ours has run at six points.

changed.unlocks: one entry on the least length of a refutation of a small pigeonhole formula in resolution over linear equations modulo two: exact proof sizes in small, the ground for running proof search exactly

changed.title: The 7 by 7 crown (u joined to v when u and v differ): some AND/OR circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 22 gates represents it
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun u v : Fin 7 => decide (u ≠ v)) 22
changed.unlocks: the crown ladder: whether one crown beats our held circuit at n = 7
changed.context: Answer with a circuit: a gate list (AND or OR, at most two wires read; wires 0 to 6 left, 7 to 13 right, gate j writes wire 14+j, each gate reads only earlier wires) and the output wire, judged on all 49 inputs with one vertex on each side. We hold 23 gates: one OR of the two vertex wires per index, then two-of-7 on those ORs by a prefix chain, 4n - 5 (computed). The 5 by 5 crown is exactly 15 and the 6 by 6 needs at least 18, both checked. We do not know whether 22 exists.
